g_policy.reason: The offer is opt-in, the copy states the reward (30 minutes of unlocked articles), the X leaves the feed, saving and sharing working, and a failure path is given.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 30 minutes of article access, which has no cash value.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an app event, the reader opening a fourth article today, and needs no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The 'adds' field puts a new cap on free article reading, which users get free today, and articles do not cost the app money per use the way model replies do.

g_brand_safety.reason: The lock panel sits over s02 Article, which is rated safe and is not a chat screen.

c1_revealed_value.reason: The reward gives the player reading time in the observed core flow f01 (Read a story), and it goes to the player.

c2_evidence.reason: 'what makes it work here' says flatly 'The app has no paywall, limit, or currency'. The model only records that none was seen on the home feed, so this is a fact about the whole app rather than a 'not seen' statement.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: No paid benefit is involved, and the reward expires after 30 minutes and is capped at 2 per day.

c5_moment.reason: The offer appears when the reader hits the limit on a fourth article, which is a moment of need.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn unit, the reward is granted only once the play is confirmed, and the trigger is a detectable app event (opening a fourth article).

c7_specific.reason: It names the s01 story cards, the s02 article reader and the reading flow of this news app.

other_concern: The whole idea depends on inventing a daily article limit the app doesn't have. That amounts to a new paywall-style gate on a free core flow, and it may hurt retention.
